extracted.intended_audience: USPTO leadership, policymakers, Congress, patent stakeholders and practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: An annual advisory report providing recommendations and evaluative criteria for USPTO patent operations, quality metrics, PTAB practices, pendency goals, IT modernization, international cooperation, finance, and related policies. Intended to guide USPTO management, Congress, and stakeholders on improving patent office performance and patent-system outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent control over HR/IT/procurement
rubrics_metrics.description: The PPAC recommends that the USPTO maintain independent control over the management and operation of its human resources, information technology and procurement functions and not expend USPTO user fees for start-up costs associated with the U.S. Department of Commerce’s Enterprise Services organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO should only participate in Enterprise Services to the extent it chooses to purchase commercial items that Enterprise Services can offer at lower cost and timelier than USPTO; oppose mandatory transfer/diversion of user fees to DOC for start-up costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retain fee-setting authority and access to fee collections
rubrics_metrics.description: The PPAC recommends that the USPTO work within the Administration and with Congress to ensure that it continues to retain its fee setting authority beyond the September 2018 expiration date and that it retains its access to all future fee collections, regardless of any government-wide sequestration or other limitation(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advise DOI/Administration and Congress to preserve USPTO's independent fee authority and uninterrupted access to fee receipts to support operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implement approved fee increases
rubrics_metrics.description: The fee increase developed as part of the 2015 fee setting review and presented in the Notice of Proposed Rule Making of October 3, 2016 should be put in place as soon as practicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act promptly to implement fees already reviewed and proposed to ensure sufficient resources for USPTO operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain patent operating reserve (~3 months)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PPAC recommended that the USPTO’s patent operating reserve be maintained at a level equivalent to approximately three months of expenditures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep an operating reserve to ensure financial stability and continuity of operations against disruptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce first-action and total pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: Commends reduction of first office action pendency from an average of 28 months in FY 2011 Q4 to an average of 16 months in FY 2017 Q4 and total application pendency from 34 to 24 months over the same period; urges continued pendency reduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue operational initiatives to further reduce pendency metrics; recognize applicants judge USPTO by timeliness of their applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt AIPA per-application pendency requirements as formal goals
rubrics_metrics.description: The PPAC recommends that the USPTO formally adopt the AIPA requirements as its pendency goals (14-month first action and 36-month total pendency per application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopting absolute per-application AIPA requirements provides applicants certainty beyond average goals like 10/20 and better aligns USPTO performance with statutory expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize Patent Term Adjustment (PTA)
rubrics_metrics.description: PTA is awarded when the USPTO examination does not meet AIPA per-application requirements and postpones patent expirations; PTA has been awarded to more than 1 out of every 2 issued patents, often substantially extending exclusivity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reduce examination delays that cause PTA because PTA harms the public by extending patent monopolies; monitor and reduce causes of PTA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality Metrics Program implementation
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopted new quality metrics (replacing prior Quality Composite Score) that provide a searchable, multidimensional data set for quality tracking, trend identification, and predictive modeling, including predictors of quality in work product, processes, and perception.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the new metrics to measure compliance statute-by-statute and for predictive analytics; ensure metrics cover work product, process, and perception dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work product assessed for statutory compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Work product is assessed based on its compliance with statutory requirements; FY2017 data showed compliance rates within or above target ranges for each statute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality measurement of examiner work product should prioritize statutory compliance as a core dimension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Master Review Form (MRF) standard criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The MRF provides a standard set of criteria to be used by reviewers from Technology Centers and OPQA to consistently document and assess quality review data in a single place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continue refining the MRF and include criteria directed at clarity of the record in updates; use MRF for consistent, comparable quality reviews across units.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity of the Record Pilot best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Analysis of the Clarity of the Record Pilot identified best practices in interview summaries, reasons for allowance, and claim interpretation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Launch follow-on pilots to identify how examination practices impact clarity; adopt identified best practices to improve record clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematic subset analysis of quality data
rubrics_metrics.description: PPAC recommends systematic surveys of data by defined subsets (for example, statute-by-statute for rejections improperly made) to detect quality issues that might be obscured by aggregate data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If issues are found (e.g., SME rejections improper in certain subsets), identify root causes and mechanisms to address them; ensure metrics can surface discrete but significant subsets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide public access to current quality measurement data
rubrics_metrics.description: The PPAC urges the USPTO to provide public access to a meaningful set of current quality measurement data because the Patent Dashboard's latest data was dated back to 2015.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publish up-to-date quality data to improve public perception and inform stakeholders' business decisions, valuations, and IP management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 101 training and guidance consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Request that the USPTO continue to update stakeholders and examiners on recent Section 101 jurisprudence, finalize MPEP updates in Section 2106 (Patent Eligible Subject Matter), and continue stakeholder outreach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review Section 101 training materials to ensure consistent application across art units; recommend every art unit have or have access to a Section 101 specialist to ensure uniform application of guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage PTAB issuance of precedential opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: PPAC encourages the PTAB to issue more precedential opinions that provide clarity on issues of current interest, such as panel expansions and handling of multiple IPR petitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use precedential opinions to provide clearer guidance to stakeholders and practitioners; update decision archives and make them more accessible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure fair, transparent PTAB processes
rubrics_metrics.description: The PTAB should remain vigilant in ensuring fair and transparent processes and proceedings in order to render well-grounded decisions, given evolving court decisions and administrative changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain outreach and education programs to help stakeholders understand evolving PTAB practices and the reasoning behind decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address multiple/serial IPR petitions and related analytics
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial PTAB data suggests many cases are single-petition but a notable share have multiple petitions; the PPAC recommends further analysis, which is slowed by current IT limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secure tools to automate analysis of multiple IPR petitions, study serial petitions' impact, and develop fair procedures for handling multiple petitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduce PTAB trial fees for small and micro entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee increases for IPRs and the lack of discounts for small/micro entities may make post-grant proceedings inaccessible to them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pursue legislation or policy changes to reduce PTAB trial fees for small and micro entities to improve access to post-grant proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modernize information technology and ensure system resilience
rubrics_metrics.description: Support USPTO's ongoing financial needs regarding IT infrastructure and recommend continued modernization by replacing legacy systems and rolling out new technology, especially to implement international initiatives like Global Dossier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in IT to enable analytics, 24/7 access for examiners, Global Dossier services, automated analyses (e.g., multiple IPR petitions), PE2E components (Patent Center, Global Dossier, CPC tools), and overall system stability and security.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expand international cooperation and work sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Support and expand Global Dossier, Collaborative Search Pilots, Patent Prosecution Highway (PPH) expansion, CPC adoption, and collaborative search/examination pilots under PCT to improve examination quality and efficiency through data exchange and work sharing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage reciprocal data access among IP5 offices, expand pilots that show quality/efficiency gains, and consider how imported prior art data affects applicant disclosure obligations under 37 CFR 1.56.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support telework and Patent Hoteling programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend legislative action to extend the Telework Enhancement Act of 2010 (TEAPP) and support, promote, and expand Patent Hoteling Program and other telework programs to maintain a diverse, dynamic workforce while preventing disruption to operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Telework programs are important recruitment and retention tools; preserve and expand them to attract talent and sustain operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Union-management collaboration and time/attendance monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Emphasize continued union-management collaboration regarding USPTO management changes so improvements can be implemented without protracted bargaining and recommend ongoing monitoring of OIG time and attendance recommendations directed to the USPTO's workforce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foster cooperative labor relations and implement attendance controls and monitoring to ensure accurate reporting and operational integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Elevate IP Attaché ranks to improve access
rubrics_metrics.description: Support raising the current mid-level rank of USPTO IP Attachés by one level to give them greater access to senior host government officials, Ambassadors, and senior industry representatives, enabling them to better accomplish their mission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate internally and with State/Commerce to effect rank changes and thereby enhance diplomatic access and effectiveness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish PTAB statistics and make charts readable and accessible
rubrics_metrics.description: The PPAC applauds the PTAB’s revised metrics and charts that are easier to read and analyze and encourages the PTAB to implement processes to review and update decision archives and make such information more accessible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Continue improving transparency through clearer metrics, searchable archives, and accessible data for practitioners and stakeholders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use case studies and post-grant outcomes for quality insights
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO reported case studies from Topic Submissions for Case Studies Program and a Post Grant Outcomes Program to derive insights on examiner compliance and other quality issues (e.g., 32% of SME rejections examined were improper or not properly explained).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage case studies and post-grant outcome analysis to identify training needs, guidance updates, and systemic quality problems; follow up with remedies where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure quality metrics include clarity/perception and detect discrete issues
rubrics_metrics.description: New quality metrics include predictors of quality in work product, processes, and perception; PPAC urges that metrics identify quality issues that may affect a discrete but significant subset of rejections that would otherwise be obscured by majority data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design metrics and reporting so they surface both aggregate trends and important outlier subsets (e.g., statute-specific or art-unit specific problems).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider balance and fairness in legislative/administrative changes
rubrics_metrics.description: When reviewing proposed legislative or administrative changes, consider effects in terms of balance and fairness to all stakeholders, efficient operation of examination, quality of patents issued, and overall costs and burdens to patent owners and participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO should engage decision makers and stakeholders to ensure changes are appropriately crafted and narrowly targeted without adversely affecting the overall patent system.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor and report filings, pendency, and backlog trends
rubrics_metrics.description: Track filing volumes and backlogs, pendency metrics (first action and total), patent term adjustment trends, and initiatives to address pendency as part of operational review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these operational metrics to guide resource allocation, hiring/retention (including telework effects), and process improvements aimed at meeting statutory and organizational goals.
